name: Kunpengopterus
sum: Wukongopterid from the Jurassic Tiaojishan Formation of Liaoning, China; K. antipollicatus (‘monkeydactyl’) had an opposable thumb.
holotype: IVPP V16047 (K. sinensis) — Tiaojishan Formation, Linglongta, Jianchang, Liaoning.
material: Almost complete skeletons with skulls; several specimens.
exceptional: Possibly regurgitated fish with the holotype; ‘Mrs T’ (ZMNH M8802), now K. antipollicatus, preserves an egg; the first known opposed thumb in a pterosaur.
biology: The opposable thumb, rare in non-mammals, suggests a grasping ability. Low bony crest behind the eyes, extended by cartilage and perhaps a skin flap.
author: Wang et al. 2010
